name: Silky Ibuki 390mm Replacement Blade
title: Silky Ibuki Replacement Blade 390mm
meta: Silky Ibuki replacement blade, 390 mm. Swap a dull or kinked blade on your Ibuki and keep the same handle and scabbard. Fit, use and care notes for tree crews.
tagline: A fresh 390 mm curved blade for the Silky Ibuki, so a tired saw cuts like new.
summary: The Silky Ibuki replacement blade is a 390 mm curved blade that drops into your existing Ibuki handle. When teeth are dull, chipped or the blade has taken a set, swapping it is faster and cheaper than buying a whole new saw.
highlights: 390 mm curved blade for the Silky Ibuki
Reuses your existing handle and scabbard
Aggressive large-tooth pattern for big pruning cuts
Impulse-hardened teeth, not meant to be filed
Quick swap with the handle hardware

p: The Ibuki is a long, fast-cutting curved saw that a lot of climbers carry for limbs that are too big for a 300 mm saw but not worth starting the top-handle for. Like any Silky, its teeth are impulse-hardened, so they stay sharp a long time but cannot be filed. Once the saw starts skating, binding or leaving a ragged cut, the blade is done.

A kinked blade is the other common reason to swap. If the saw has been pinched in a cut and now wobbles or tracks off line, replace it rather than trying to straighten it. You can find other blades in replacement saw blades.

A long blade like this one is worth the swap because the handle, scabbard and your feel for the saw stay the same. Climbers who run an Ibuki for big pruning cuts often keep a spare blade on the truck so a kinked or dulled blade does not end the day early.

Match the length to your handle before you order: this blade is the 390 mm size. Remove the handle hardware, seat the new blade fully, and snug the fasteners so there is no play. Wear gloves while handling it, because a new Silky blade is very sharp.

Wipe sap off after the day's work and give the blade a light coat of oil if it will sit for a while. Keep it in the scabbard on the saddle so the teeth are covered when you move through the tree and when the saw rides in the truck.

faq.q: Can I sharpen a Silky Ibuki blade?
faq.a: Not practically. The teeth are impulse-hardened, which keeps them sharp for a long time but makes filing ineffective. Replace the blade when it dulls.

faq.q: Will this blade fit other Silky saws?
faq.a: It is made for the Silky Ibuki 390 mm. Check the model and length of your saw before ordering, because Silky blades are model-specific.

name: Silky Zubat Arborist Edition Replacement Blade
title: Silky Zubat Replacement Blade, Arborist Edition
h1: Silky Zubat Replacement Blade, Arborist Edition
meta: Silky Zubat replacement blade, Arborist Edition. Restore a dull or bent Zubat with a fresh curved blade that fits your current handle. Fit and care tips inside.
tagline: A new curved blade for the Zubat Arborist Edition, the saw many climbers live with.
summary: This Silky Zubat replacement blade is made for the Zubat Arborist Edition, so you keep the handle and scabbard you already trust. It is the simple fix when a favorite saw starts cutting slow or wandering.
highlights: Replacement for the Zubat Arborist Edition
Curved blade that pulls into the cut
Impulse-hardened teeth stay sharp a long time
Keeps your existing handle and scabbard
Cheaper than replacing the whole saw

p: The Zubat is one of the most common hand saws on a climbing saddle because the curved blade pulls itself into the wood and the cut stays clean for pruning. Used every day, though, the teeth wear down. When you notice more strokes per cut, a rougher finish, or the saw drifting, it is time for a new blade.

Blades also get kinked when a limb settles and pinches the saw. A bent blade will not track straight and can bind hard, so swap it rather than fight it. See the rest of our saw blades for other models.

Confirm that your saw is the Arborist Edition before ordering, since Silky blades are specific to model and length. Install the blade with the handle hardware fully seated and tight, and wear gloves while you do it.

After use, knock off sap and sawdust, let the blade dry, and keep it sheathed. A clean blade cuts faster and resists rust, and a covered blade is safer for you and your rope when moving around the tree.

If you run several Zubats across a crew, keeping one or two spare blades on the truck means nobody is stuck with a dull saw halfway through a pruning job. Swapping takes a few minutes with the right driver, and the climber goes back up with a saw that cuts the way it did on day one.

faq.q: Does this fit the standard Zubat?
faq.a: It is listed for the Zubat Arborist Edition. Check your saw's model and blade length against the replacement before ordering.

faq.q: How do I know the blade is worn out?
faq.a: Slow cutting, a ragged finish, more effort per stroke, or a saw that wanders off line are the usual signs. A bent blade should be replaced right away.

name: Jameson Folding Tri-Cut Hand Saw
title: Jameson Folding Tri-Cut Hand Saw
meta: Jameson Folding Tri-Cut Hand Saw for pruning and brush work. It folds closed for a pocket or pouch and cuts on the pull stroke. Uses, care and buying notes.
tagline: A compact folding pruning saw with a Tri-Cut blade for ground and light climbing work.
summary: The Jameson Folding Tri-Cut Hand Saw uses a Tri-Cut tooth pattern that cuts on the pull stroke and clears chips well in green wood. It folds closed, so it rides in a pocket or pouch without a scabbard.
highlights: Tri-Cut teeth for fast pull-stroke cutting
Good for small limbs, suckers and brush
Easy to carry on the ground crew

p: A folding saw is the one you keep in your pocket for small jobs: clearing suckers, cutting a branch that caught in the chipper chute, trimming a shrub while the climber is up. The Jameson folding Tri-Cut is light and cheap enough that losing one does not ruin the day.

The Tri-Cut pattern has three bevels on each tooth and cuts on the pull, so you are not pushing a thin blade into the wood. For bigger limbs or full-time climbing, step up to a fixed blade from our hand saws and scabbards.

Ground workers like having a folder on them because there is always a small cut to make between loads: a branch that will not lie flat on the brush pile, a root in the way of a stump grinder, or a stub left behind after a limb comes down. A folding saw handles those jobs without walking back to the truck.
Make sure the blade is fully open and locked before cutting, and keep your free hand out of the cut line. Close the saw when you are done rather than tossing it open into a bucket or truck bed.

Wipe off sap and moisture at the end of the day. If the pivot gets stiff, clean it and add a drop of light oil. When the teeth go dull, replacing the saw is usually more practical than trying to file a hardened pruning blade.

faq.q: Is a folding saw good for climbing?
faq.a: It works for light pruning, but many climbers prefer a fixed-blade saw in a scabbard because it is quicker to draw and put away with one hand.

faq.q: What does Tri-Cut mean?
faq.a: It is a tooth pattern with three cutting edges per tooth that cuts on the pull stroke and clears chips well in green wood.

name: Jameson Hand Saw with Scabbard
title: Jameson Hand Saw with Scabbard
meta: Jameson hand saw with scabbard for pruning, climbing and ground work. A fixed blade that cuts on the pull and a sheath for your belt or saddle. Details here.
tagline: A fixed-blade pruning saw that comes with its own scabbard, ready for the saddle.
summary: The Jameson hand saw with scabbard is a fixed-blade pruning saw sold with a matching sheath, so it is ready to clip on and work. It is a practical choice for ground crews and climbers who want a dependable saw without a premium price.
highlights: Fixed blade for stiff, straight cuts
Rides on a belt or climbing saddle
Good value for crews outfitting several people

body.h: A working saw, ready to carry
p: A fixed-blade saw is quicker than a folder when you are cutting all day: draw it, make the cut, put it back. Having the scabbard included means you are not shopping for a separate sheath that may or may not fit the blade.

This saw suits ground workers cleaning up brush, climbers doing light to medium pruning, and crews that want spare saws on the truck. For other blade lengths and premium Japanese saws, see hand saws and scabbards.

Crews buying for several people like a saw and scabbard sold together because the fit is known and setup is quick. New ground workers can learn on a solid, affordable saw before moving to a premium blade, and an experienced climber can keep one as a spare on the truck for days when the main saw is out of service.
Clip the scabbard where you can reach it with either hand and where it will not snag your climbing line. Always sheath the saw before you move in the tree or walk across the site.

Keep the blade clean of sap and dry before it goes back in the scabbard. Empty sawdust from the sheath now and then so the blade seats fully. Replace the saw or blade when it cuts slowly or a tooth breaks.

When the blade gets dull or a tooth snaps, look at replacing the saw rather than filing it. Pruning teeth are hardened for long life, and a sharp saw is safer than one you have to force through the wood.

faq.q: Does the scabbard come with the saw?
faq.a: Yes. This listing is the saw and its scabbard together.

faq.q: Can I use it from the saddle?
faq.a: Yes. Clip the scabbard to a saddle attachment point or belt where it is easy to reach and stays clear of your rope.

name: Silky Tsurugi Curved Hand Saw, Large Teeth, 330mm
title: Silky Tsurugi Curved Hand Saw, 330mm Large Teeth
h1: Silky Tsurugi Curved Hand Saw, Large Teeth, 330mm
meta: Silky Tsurugi curved hand saw with a 330 mm blade and large teeth for fast pruning cuts on bigger limbs. How it compares, who it suits and how to care for it.
tagline: A 330 mm curved Silky with large teeth for fast cuts on thicker limbs.
summary: The Silky Tsurugi curved hand saw pairs a 330 mm blade with large teeth, so it moves through thicker green limbs quickly. It is a strong pick for climbers who prune bigger wood and want a fixed curved saw in a scabbard.
highlights: Large teeth for speed in green wood

body.h: What the Tsurugi is good at
p: The curve on the Tsurugi pulls the blade into the wood on the draw stroke, which helps when you are reaching overhead or cutting at an awkward angle from a climbing position. Large teeth remove more wood per stroke, so this setup is about speed in green limbs rather than a fine finish.
At 330 mm it sits in the middle of Silky's range: long enough for real limbs, short enough to ride on a saddle all day. Compare it with other models in hand saws and scabbards.

Large teeth do leave a rougher surface than fine or medium teeth. For most removal and heavy pruning cuts that does not matter, and the speed saves effort over a long day. If most of your work is detail pruning on ornamentals, a finer tooth may suit you better.
Let the saw do the work. Long, smooth strokes are faster and keep the blade from binding. Support or undercut limbs where needed so the kerf does not close on the blade.
Silky teeth are hardened and cannot be filed, so when the blade dulls, fit a replacement blade. Clean sap off at the end of the day and keep the saw sheathed whenever you are moving in the tree.
Keep an eye on the scabbard as well as the blade. A worn sheath lets the tip poke through and can catch your rope or leg.

faq.q: Large teeth or medium teeth?
faq.a: Large teeth cut faster in green wood and bigger limbs. Medium or fine teeth leave a smoother cut and suit smaller, drier or precision pruning.

faq.q: Is the 330 mm too long for climbing?
faq.a: Most climbers find 330 mm a comfortable all-round length. Very tight crowns may favor a shorter saw.

name: Jameson Vinyl Pruner and Pole Bag
keyword: jameson vinyl pruner and pole bag
title: Jameson Vinyl Pruner and Pole Bag
h1: Jameson Vinyl Pruner and Pole Bag
meta: Jameson vinyl pruner and pole bag for storing pole sections, pruner heads and saw heads. Keeps blades covered and the kit together in the truck. Tips inside.
tagline: A vinyl bag that keeps pole sections, pruner heads and saw heads together.
summary: The Jameson vinyl pruner and pole bag is a carry bag for sectional poles, pruner heads and pole saw heads. It keeps a pole kit in one place and keeps sharp heads covered when the gear rides in the truck.
highlights: Keeps a kit together on the truck
specs: Pole sections, pruner and saw heads

p: Loose pole sections rattle around a truck bed, get scratched, and go missing. A pole saw head bouncing around uncovered is a cut waiting to happen. A dedicated bag keeps the whole kit together, so the ground worker can grab one bag and have everything needed to reach a limb.
For fiberglass poles, avoiding deep scratches and gouges also matters for the pole itself. Find matching poles and heads in poles and kits.

A good bag also makes it obvious when something is missing. If the bag is the only place pole gear lives, the crew can check at a glance that every section, head and blade guard came back from the job, instead of finding out at the next site that a section was left leaning against a fence.

Put saw heads in with the blade guard or scabbard on, and seat pruner heads so the cutting edge faces away from your hands when you reach in. Wipe sap and mud off before storage so it does not build up inside.
Vinyl wipes clean with mild soap and water. Let the bag and poles dry before closing it up for a long stretch, and check the seams and closure now and then so nothing slides out on the road.
Label the bag with your company name or crew number if several trucks carry similar kits.

faq.q: Will it fit both poles and pruner heads?
faq.a: Yes. It is made to carry pole sections together with pruner and saw heads.

faq.q: Should I store fiberglass poles wet?
faq.a: No. Wipe them clean and let them dry before long storage to keep the surface in good shape.

name: Jameson LS Kit: Pole Saw and LS Poles
title: Jameson LS Pole Saw Kit with LS Poles
h1: Jameson LS Pole Saw Kit with LS Poles
meta: Jameson LS pole saw kit with a saw head and LS fiberglass pole sections for reaching limbs from the ground. What comes in it and how to use and care for it.
tagline: A ready-to-work Jameson pole saw head with LS fiberglass pole sections.
summary: The Jameson LS pole saw kit pairs a pole saw head with Jameson LS pole sections, so you have a complete reach tool out of the box. It suits ground workers and climbers who need to cut limbs above head height without a powered pole saw.
highlights: Pole saw head plus LS pole sections
specs: Pole saw head and LS pole sections

p: A manual pole saw is still the right tool for a lot of pruning: deadwood off a roof line, raising a canopy over a sidewalk, or cutting a hanger the climber cannot reach. It is quiet, light compared with a powered pole saw, and there is nothing to start.
This kit gives you a saw head and LS poles that join together, so you can build the length you need. Add pruner heads or extra sections from pole saws and scabbards.

A kit also means the parts are made to work together. The saw head seats on the pole the way it was designed to, the joints match, and you are not finding out on the job that a head from one brand rattles on a pole from another. For crews outfitting a new truck, that saves time and returns.

Look up before you raise a pole. Keep well clear of overhead power lines and follow your company's minimum approach distances; a fiberglass pole that is dirty or wet should not be treated as insulating. Wear a helmet and eye protection, because cut material falls toward you.
Stand to the side of the limb, not under it, and pull with smooth strokes. Wipe the poles clean after use and store them dry in a pole bag. Check joints and the saw head bolt before each job.
Replace dull or bent blades rather than forcing them, and keep a spare blade in the pole bag.

faq.q: Can I add more pole sections?
faq.a: Yes. Additional Jameson sections can extend reach. Use sections from the same system so the joints lock properly.

faq.q: Are fiberglass poles safe near power lines?
faq.a: Do not rely on them for protection. Keep the required clearance from lines and follow utility and ANSI Z133 rules.

name: Pole Saw Kit: Saw Head and 16 in Tri-Cut Blade
title: Pole Saw Head Kit with 16 in Tri-Cut Blade
h1: Pole Saw Head Kit with 16 in Tri-Cut Blade
meta: Pole saw head kit with a 16 in Tri-Cut blade that mounts on standard pruning poles. Cuts on the pull for fast reach pruning from the ground. Fit and care notes.
tagline: A pole saw head and 16 in Tri-Cut blade to put on your own poles.
summary: This pole saw head kit combines a mounting head with a 16 in Tri-Cut blade, ready to fit on your pruning poles. It is a simple way to turn an existing pole into a reach saw or to replace a worn head.
highlights: Replaces a worn or broken head

p: The kit is a saw head that fits on a pole plus a 16 in Tri-Cut blade. Sixteen inches is a common working length: long enough for real limbs, short enough to control at the end of several pole sections. The Tri-Cut teeth cut on the pull, which is how you naturally work a pole saw from the ground.
Check that the head matches the fitting on your poles before ordering. Poles and complete kits are in pole saws and scabbards.

Replacing the head and blade together is often the cleanest fix when an old head is cracked, the bolt holes are worn or the blade has been bent one too many times. You get a fresh, matched setup without replacing the poles that are still in good shape.

Start the cut with short strokes to set the kerf, then use the full blade. On larger limbs, a small undercut first helps stop bark tearing back toward the trunk. Stand off to one side so the limb does not drop on you.
Keep clear of power lines, wear a helmet and eye protection, and keep a blade guard on whenever the saw is not cutting. Replace the blade when it dulls or bends.
Store the saw with a guard on the blade and in a pole bag, so the teeth stay sharp and nobody grabs it by the wrong end.

faq.q: Will this fit my poles?
faq.a: It is made for standard pruning pole fittings. Compare the head's connection with your pole before buying.

faq.q: Can I replace just the blade later?
faq.a: Yes. Replacement Tri-Cut blades are sold separately, so you can keep the head and swap the blade.

name: Weaver Pruner Pouch with Clip, 8 in
title: Weaver Pruner Pouch with Clip, 8 in
h1: Weaver Pruner Pouch with Clip, 8 in
meta: Weaver pruner pouch with clip, 8 in size. Carries hand pruners on a belt or saddle so they are ready to grab and safely stowed. Fit, carry and care tips here.
tagline: A clip-on 8 in pouch that keeps your hand pruners on your hip.
summary: The Weaver pruner pouch with clip holds a pair of hand pruners on a belt or saddle, ready for quick cuts. It is a small piece of kit, but it stops pruners getting dropped, lost or left open in a pocket.
highlights: Clip attaches to belt or saddle

body.h: Why carry pruners in a pouch
p: Pruners get used dozens of times a day on a pruning job: suckers, small deadwood, clean-up cuts. Keeping them in a pouch on your hip means you are not digging in a pocket or climbing back down because they fell out. The clip moves easily between your belt and saddle.
Check that your pruners fit an 8 in pouch before ordering. Scabbards and other pouches are in pole saws and scabbards.

Weaver has made climbing and arborist gear for a long time, and its pouches are built for daily use rather than occasional garden work. A pruner pouch is cheap insurance against dropping a pair of pruners from height, which is both a nuisance and a hazard to the ground crew working below.
Mount the pouch on the side opposite your saw scabbard so the two do not crowd each other, and away from where your climbing line runs. Always close the pruners before they go in the pouch.
Shake out sawdust and leaves regularly. If the pouch gets soaked, let it air dry rather than drying it next to a heater.
Ground workers can wear one too. Having pruners on your hip while dragging brush means small cleanup cuts get done on the spot instead of being left for later.

faq.q: Will my pruners fit?
faq.a: It suits most standard bypass hand pruners that fit an 8 in pouch. Measure the closed length of your pruners.

faq.q: Can I attach it to a climbing saddle?
faq.a: Yes. Clip it to a saddle gear loop or belt where it stays clear of your rope and life-support connections.

name: Weaver Saw Scabbard, Curved Back, with Pruner Pouch (HL 14)
title: Weaver Saw Scabbard with Pruner Pouch, HL 14
h1: Weaver Saw Scabbard, Curved Back, with Pruner Pouch (HL 14)
meta: Weaver saw scabbard with a curved back and pruner pouch, HL 14. Carries a 14 in hand saw and pruners together on one belt or saddle mount. Fit and care notes.
tagline: One scabbard for a 14 in hand saw with a pouch for your pruners.
summary: The Weaver saw scabbard with pruner pouch carries a 14 in hand saw and a pair of pruners in one holster. The curved back follows the shape of a curved pruning saw, and the combined design saves space on a belt or saddle.

p: Most pruning climbers carry a hand saw and pruners. Putting both in one scabbard frees up space on the saddle and keeps the cutting tools together on one side. The curved back matches curved saws, so the blade sits in the sheath without binding.
Match the HL 14 size to a 14 in blade. Other sizes and styles are in pole saws and scabbards.

A combined holster is a good fit for production pruning, where you switch between saw and pruners many times on each limb. Both tools are in the same place every time, so your hand finds them without looking, and you have one less item to clip on and off the saddle at the start and end of the day.

Mount the scabbard where you can draw and replace the saw with your dominant hand without looking, and where the saw tip will not catch your climbing line or lanyard. Always sheath the saw before moving in the tree.
Clean out sawdust and sap so the blade seats fully. Check stitching and the mount regularly, and replace the scabbard if the saw tip starts to poke through.
Ground workers can wear it on a belt to keep both tools handy while cleaning up.

faq.q: What saw length does HL 14 fit?
faq.a: It is sized for 14 in hand saw blades. Check your blade length before ordering.

faq.q: Does it work with straight saws?
faq.a: It is shaped for curved saws. A straight-back scabbard is a better fit for straight blades.

name: Weaver Saw Scabbard, Curved Back, with Snap, Rubberized (HL 14)
title: Weaver Rubberized Saw Scabbard with Snap, HL 14
h1: Weaver Rubberized Saw Scabbard with Snap (HL 14)
meta: Weaver rubberized saw scabbard with a snap and curved back, sized HL 14 for 14 in hand saws. Holds the saw securely on a belt or saddle. Fit and care tips.
tagline: A rubberized 14 in curved scabbard with a snap to keep the saw in place.
summary: This Weaver rubberized saw scabbard has a curved back and a snap closure for 14 in hand saws. It holds a curved pruning saw securely on a belt or saddle and sheds water and sap better than bare material.

body.h: A secure home for your saw
p: A saw that drops out of its scabbard is a hazard to the people below. The snap on this scabbard adds retention, and the rubberized finish stands up to wet days, sap and rough handling. The curved back matches curved pruning saws so the blade slides in without binding.
This is the HL 14 size for 14 in blades. Other scabbards and pole saw gear are in pole saws and scabbards.

A rubberized scabbard is a sensible choice for crews that work through wet seasons or in sappy species like pine. Water and pitch wipe off the surface rather than soaking in, and the sheath holds its shape longer than one that gets soaked and dried over and over.
Place the scabbard where you can reach it with either hand if possible, and away from your climbing line and lanyard. Close the snap whenever you move in the tree or walk the site.
Rinse off sap and grit and let it dry. Check the snap and mount from time to time, and replace the scabbard if the saw tip starts to wear through.
If you carry the saw on a belt on the ground, the snap is just as useful when you bend, kneel and drag brush all day.

faq.q: What is the snap for?
faq.a: It helps hold the saw in the scabbard while you climb, so the saw does not slide out when you are upside down or moving.

faq.q: Which saws fit?
faq.a: Curved hand saws with a 14 in blade. Measure your blade before ordering.

name: Jameson 4 ft Hollow Core Pole
title: Jameson Hollow Core Pole, 4 ft Fiberglass Section
meta: Jameson hollow core pole, 4 ft fiberglass section for pole saws and pruners. Add reach to a pole kit or replace a damaged section. Fit, use and care notes here.
tagline: A 4 ft fiberglass pole section to build or extend a Jameson pole kit.
summary: The Jameson hollow core pole is a 4 ft fiberglass section for pole saw and pruner setups. Use it to extend your reach or replace a damaged section in an existing kit.
highlights: Takes pole saw or pruner heads

p: Sectional poles let you carry a short kit and build length on site. A 4 ft section is handy for fine-tuning reach, and it is light enough that adding one does not make the pole feel like a log at the top.
Make sure the joint style matches your other sections and heads before ordering. Complete kits and other sections are in poles and kits.

Short sections are also useful for working under a low canopy or in tight spaces between buildings, where a long section is clumsy to handle. Many crews carry a mix of section lengths so they can build exactly the reach they need without the pole sticking out far behind them.

Keep the required distance from power lines. A fiberglass pole should not be counted on for electrical protection, especially when dirty or wet. Wear a helmet and eye protection when cutting overhead.
Wipe poles clean after use, inspect for cracks, splits or crushed ends, and retire any damaged section. Store them dry and out of direct sun when possible.

Hollow core poles are lighter than solid or foam-filled poles of the same length, which helps with control at full extension. Treat them gently in the truck, because a crushed end or a deep gouge can weaken the section.

faq.q: Is a hollow core pole insulated?
faq.a: Do not rely on it for electrical protection. Follow minimum approach distances and utility rules around lines.

faq.q: Will it join my existing poles?
faq.a: It joins compatible Jameson sections. Check your current joint style before buying.

name: Jameson 6 ft B-Lite Poles
title: Jameson B-Lite Pole, 6 ft Fiberglass Section
meta: Jameson B-Lite pole, a 6 ft light fiberglass section for pole saws and pruners. Extend a kit or replace a worn section. How it fits and how to care for it.
tagline: A light 6 ft Jameson pole section for pole saws and pruners.
summary: The Jameson B-Lite pole is a 6 ft lightweight fiberglass section for building pole saw and pruner kits. Longer sections mean fewer joints for the same reach, and the light build helps when you are working overhead for hours.

p: Every joint in a pole adds a little flex and a little weight. Six foot sections let you reach high with fewer joints, and the B-Lite build keeps the pole manageable when it is fully extended. That matters on a long day of raising canopies or clearing deadwood from the ground.
Confirm the joint type matches your other sections and heads. More options are in poles and kits.

For crews doing clearance work along streets and driveways, being able to reach higher with a lighter pole makes a real difference by the end of the week. Less weight at the top means better control of the head, cleaner cuts and less strain on shoulders and back.
Look up before raising a pole and stay well clear of energized lines; do not treat fiberglass as protection. Wear a helmet and eyewear, and stand off to the side of the limb you are cutting.
Wipe the pole clean after use and check for cracks, splintering or damaged ends. Retire a damaged section. Store poles dry and in a bag to protect the surface.
Keep a record of how many sections each truck carries so a missing one is noticed quickly.

faq.q: How many sections do I need?
faq.a: It depends on the height you work at. Add sections until you can reach comfortably while standing off to the side of the cut.

faq.q: Can I mix B-Lite with other Jameson poles?
faq.a: Sections with matching joints can be combined. Check the joint style before mixing.

name: Husqvarna 32 in Lopper
title: Husqvarna Lopper, 32 in: Uses and Care
meta: Husqvarna lopper with 32 in handles for cutting branches too thick for hand pruners. Good leverage for shrub and small-tree work. Uses, care and buying notes.
tagline: A 32 in lopper with the leverage for branches too thick for hand pruners.
summary: The Husqvarna lopper with 32 in handles gives you the leverage to cut branches that are too thick for hand pruners. It is a ground-crew staple for shrub work, small-tree pruning and clean-up around the job.

body.h: Where a lopper earns its place
p: Loppers sit between hand pruners and a saw. They make quick work of branches on shrubs, small trees and sucker growth, and they are faster than a saw for a lot of small cuts. The 32 in length gives good leverage and a bit of reach into a shrub without bending over.
For smaller stems use hand pruners, and for bigger wood reach for a saw. Compare options in pruners and loppers.

On tree jobs, loppers are mostly a ground tool. They speed up processing brush for the chipper, trimming small limbs off logs and clearing access around the work area. A lopper is also handy for landscape crews working shrubs and hedges between tree work.

body.h: Cutting well and keeping it sharp
p: Get the branch deep into the jaws, close to the pivot, for the most cutting power. Do not twist the lopper to finish a cut; that springs the blades and dulls the edge. If a branch will not cut cleanly, switch to a saw.
Clean sap off the blades after use and keep the pivot lightly oiled. Touch up the cutting edge with a file or stone as it dulls, and keep the bolt adjusted so the blades pass cleanly.
Keep the lopper with the hand tools in the truck so it does not end up under the logs or brush pile.

faq.q: What size branch can it cut?
faq.a: Loppers are for branches too thick for hand pruners but still small enough to close the jaws on easily. If you have to strain or twist, use a saw.

faq.q: Lopper or pole pruner?
faq.a: A lopper is for work within arm's reach. For higher limbs from the ground, use a pole pruner.

name: Husqvarna Technical Hand Pruner
title: Husqvarna Technical Hand Pruner
meta: Husqvarna Technical hand pruner for clean cuts on small branches and shrubs. Fits a pouch for climbers and ground crews. What it is for and how to care for it.
tagline: A pocket-size hand pruner for clean cuts on small stems all day.
summary: The Husqvarna Technical hand pruner is built for clean, repeated cuts on small branches, suckers and shrub growth. It rides in a pruner pouch so climbers and ground workers have it ready.

p: On a pruning job, hand pruners make more cuts than anything else: suckers, water sprouts, small deadwood and clean-up of torn stubs. A good pruner closes smoothly, cuts without crushing, and sits comfortably in the hand for hundreds of cuts.
Keep it in a pouch on your saddle or belt so it does not end up on the ground. Other pruners and loppers are in pruners and loppers.

Climbers use hand pruners for fine pruning work that would be slow or untidy with a saw, such as removing small crossing branches, tidying cut ends, and reducing small twigs back to a lateral. Ground workers use them for shrub work and for cleaning up brush before it goes into the chipper.
Wipe sap from the blades during the day; it builds up quickly and makes the pruner stick. Oil the pivot and spring now and then, and keep the pivot bolt adjusted so the blades meet cleanly.
Hone the cutting edge as it dulls. If you work in diseased trees, clean the blades between trees as your plant health practices require.
Keep a spare pair in the truck. Pruners get dropped and lost more than any other tool, and having a backup keeps the job moving.

faq.q: What size branches is it for?
faq.a: Small stems and twigs you can close the pruner on easily. Use a lopper or saw for thicker wood.

faq.q: Should I disinfect between trees?
faq.a: Where disease spread is a concern, clean and disinfect blades between trees as recommended for that disease.

name: Jameson Big Mouth Double Pulley Pruner with Adapter and Rope
title: Jameson Big Mouth Double Pulley Pruner
h1: Jameson Big Mouth Double Pulley Pruner with Adapter and Rope
meta: Jameson Big Mouth pruner with a double pulley, pole adapter and rope. A wide jaw and extra pulling power for thicker limbs from the ground. Fit and care tips.
tagline: A wide-jaw pole pruner head with double pulley power, adapter and rope included.
summary: The Jameson Big Mouth pruner is a pole pruner head with a wide jaw and a double pulley for extra cutting power, sold with a pole adapter and pull rope. It is aimed at ground workers who want to cut thicker limbs on a pole without switching to a saw.

p: A pole pruner makes clean cuts on limbs above your head without climbing. The Big Mouth has a wider jaw than a standard head, so it takes thicker wood, and the double pulley multiplies the force on the rope so you are not hanging off it to finish a cut.
With the adapter and rope included, you just need poles. Find poles and other heads in pruners and loppers.

That extra capacity means fewer trips back to the truck for a pole saw when a limb is a little too big for a standard pruner. Pruner cuts are also cleaner than many saw cuts on small limbs, which matters for good pruning practice on ornamental trees and street trees.
Set the jaw fully over the limb and pull smoothly. Stand to the side so the cut piece does not drop on you, and wear a helmet and eye protection. Keep well clear of power lines.

Clean sap off the blade, oil the pivot and pulleys, and check the rope for wear and fraying. Replace a worn rope before it breaks mid-cut, and sharpen or replace the blade when cuts start to crush rather than slice.
Keep the rope coiled and out of the way while working so nobody trips on it, and keep it clear of the cutting head when storing the pruner.

faq.q: Do I need to buy poles separately?
faq.a: Yes. This listing is the pruner head with adapter and rope. Add compatible poles to build the reach you need.

faq.q: What does the double pulley do?
faq.a: It gives more mechanical advantage than a single pulley, so you need less pull on the rope to make a cut.

name: Jameson CompositLock Pruner Head
title: Jameson CompositLock Pruner Head
meta: Jameson CompositLock pruner head for mounting on compatible Jameson poles. Cuts overhead limbs cleanly from the ground. Fit, safe use and care notes here.
tagline: A Jameson pole pruner head with the CompositLock connection.
summary: The Jameson CompositLock pruner head mounts on compatible Jameson poles to cut limbs overhead from the ground. Use it to build a new pole pruner or replace a worn head on an existing kit.
highlights: Cuts overhead limbs from the ground

p: A pruner head turns a pole into a clean-cutting tool for limbs you cannot reach from the ground. It is the right choice for smaller limbs where a saw is overkill and a clean cut matters, such as raising a canopy or removing small deadwood.
The CompositLock fitting must match your poles, so check before you order. Other heads and pruners are in pruners and loppers.

Replacing just the head makes sense when the poles are still in good shape but the old head is worn, bent or missing parts. A fresh head with a sharp blade and smooth pivot cuts more cleanly and takes less effort on the rope, which makes a big difference on a long day of clearance pruning.
Wear a helmet and eye protection and stand to the side of the cut. Keep clear of power lines; do not count on a pole for electrical protection.
Keep the blade clean and sharp, oil the pivot and pulley, and check the rope and fittings before each job. Replace worn rope and damaged parts promptly.

Keep the pruner head covered and stored in a pole bag when it is not in use, so the blade stays sharp and nobody grabs it by the cutting end. A spare blade and rope in the bag can save a trip back to the shop.

faq.q: Does this include rope and poles?
faq.a: This listing is the pruner head. Check the product details for included rope, and add poles separately.

faq.q: Will it fit non-Jameson poles?
faq.a: It is designed for the CompositLock connection. Confirm your pole fitting before buying.

name: Jameson Heavy Duty Pruner
title: Jameson Heavy Duty Pruner Head for Pole Pruning
meta: Jameson heavy duty pruner head for pole pruning on thicker limbs. A tough head for crews who cut overhead all day from the ground. Fit, use and care notes here.
tagline: A tough Jameson pole pruner head for crews who cut overhead all day.
summary: The Jameson heavy duty pruner is a pole pruner head built for steady professional use on overhead limbs. It suits crews that want a durable head for daily canopy raising and clearance work.

p: Pole pruners on a busy crew take a beating: dropped in the truck, banged into limbs, pulled hard on wet days. A heavy duty head stands up to that and keeps cutting cleanly. It is a good fit for clearance pruning, line-of-sight work and canopy raising.
Match the head to your pole connection and add rope if needed. Compare heads in pruners and loppers.

Pole pruners are the right tool for small limbs that need a clean cut, especially on street trees and ornamentals. They are quiet, need no fuel, and are easy to hand to a ground worker. A heavy duty head gives you that clean cut and holds up to the knocks of daily work.
Seat the limb fully in the jaw before pulling, stand off to the side, and wear a helmet and eye protection. Keep the required clearance from power lines.
Clean and oil the pivot and pulley, keep the blade sharp, and inspect the rope for wear. Replace worn parts before they fail on the job.

Keep a spare blade and rope with the kit so a worn part does not stop the job. Store the pruner in a pole bag with the cutting head covered, and keep it out of the bottom of the truck where heavy gear can bend it.

faq.q: Does it come with a rope?
faq.a: Check the listing details. Pruner heads are often sold without poles, and rope may be separate.

faq.q: Can the blade be replaced?
faq.a: Jameson pruner heads are serviceable, and replacement blades are available for common models.

name: Jameson JA-14 Fixed Pulley Pruner Kit
title: Jameson JA-14 Fixed Pulley Pruner Kit
h1: Jameson JA-14 Fixed Pulley Pruner Kit
meta: Jameson JA-14 pruner kit with a fixed pulley pruner head and poles, ready to cut overhead limbs from the ground. What is in it and how to use and care for it.
tagline: A complete Jameson pole pruner kit built around a fixed pulley head.
summary: The Jameson JA-14 pruner kit is a complete pole pruner setup built around a fixed pulley pruner head. It gives a ground crew everything needed to make clean overhead cuts without piecing a kit together.
highlights: Ready to work out of the box
Clean overhead cuts from the ground

body.h: A kit that is ready to go
p: Buying a kit saves you matching heads, adapters, poles and rope from different listings. The JA-14 is built around a fixed pulley pruner, a simple and dependable design for clean cuts on smaller overhead limbs.
Pair it with a pole saw head for bigger wood. Other kits and heads are in pruners and loppers.

For a new crew member, a complete kit is also easier to learn with. The pruner, poles and rope all work together, so the focus can stay on how to position the head, how to pull smoothly, and where to stand while the cut piece falls. Once that is mastered, adding a saw head or more sections is easy.
Look up and check for power lines before raising the pole, and keep the required distance. Wear a helmet and eye protection and stand to the side of the limb.
After the job, wipe the poles and head clean, oil the pivot and pulley, and check the rope for wear. Store the kit dry, ideally in a pole bag.

Check that the pole joints lock fully before raising the pole, and do not use the pole as a lever or pry bar. Replace any pole section that is cracked or split, and keep a spare rope in the bag in case the main one wears through.

faq.q: Fixed pulley or double pulley?
faq.a: A fixed single pulley is simple and fine for smaller limbs. A double pulley gives more cutting force for thicker wood.

faq.q: Can I add poles to this kit?
faq.a: Yes. Compatible Jameson sections can be added for more reach.

name: Notch Rope Runner Vertec Aeris Friction Body Kit
title: Notch Rope Runner Friction Body Kit
h1: Notch Rope Runner Vertec Aeris Friction Body Kit
meta: Notch Rope Runner friction body kit to keep your mechanical friction device in service. Replace worn friction parts as Notch directs. Fit and inspection notes.
tagline: Replacement friction parts to keep a Notch Rope Runner in service.
summary: This Notch Rope Runner friction body kit supplies replacement friction parts for the Rope Runner family of mechanical climbing devices. Friction parts wear with every descent, and replacing them as the maker directs keeps the device working as designed.
highlights: Replacement friction parts for the Rope Runner
For trained MRS and SRS climbers

p: Every time you descend on a mechanical friction device, the rope runs over the friction surfaces and slowly wears them. As the surfaces wear, the device can behave differently, and eventually the parts reach the maker's wear limit. A friction body kit lets you replace those parts instead of the whole device.
Check the kit against your exact Rope Runner model before ordering. Other MRS devices are in devices for MRS.

Keeping a device in service with genuine replacement parts is usually much cheaper than buying a new one, and it means you keep a tool you already know how to use. Climbers who descend a lot, or who work on gritty or sandy rope, will wear friction parts faster and should check them more often.

body.h: Fit and inspect by the book
p: Replace parts only as Notch's instructions describe, and if you are not confident doing it, have a competent person do it. After fitting, check function on the ground before climbing.
Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every use, and be used only by trained climbers working to ANSI Z133.
Keep records of when parts were replaced, along with the device's inspection history. If anything about the kit or your device is unclear, contact the maker or your supplier before climbing on it.

faq.q: How do I know the friction parts are worn?
faq.a: Compare them with the wear indicators or limits in the Notch instructions. Grooving or changes in how the device holds and releases are warning signs.

faq.q: Can I fit the kit myself?
faq.a: Follow the maker's instructions exactly. If you are not sure, have a competent person service the device.

name: Rock Exotica Akimbo 2
title: Rock Exotica Akimbo 2 Rope Access Device for SRS
meta: Rock Exotica Akimbo 2, a mechanical friction device for SRS and MRS tree climbing with smooth, adjustable control. How it works, who it suits and what to check.
tagline: A mechanical friction device for SRS and MRS climbing with smooth, adjustable control.
summary: The Rock Exotica Akimbo 2 is a mechanical friction device for stationary rope (SRS) and moving rope (MRS) tree climbing. Climbers choose it for smooth descents and for being able to adjust friction to suit their rope and the conditions.
highlights: Made by Rock Exotica in the USA

p: The Akimbo replaces a friction hitch with a mechanical device, which means less tending, more consistent friction and less heat on your rope. Being able to adjust friction is useful as your rope ages, on wet days, or when switching between ropes.
It works in both SRS and MRS setups, so one device can cover most of your climbing. Compare it with other devices in devices for SRS.

For climbers moving from a hitch to a mechanical device, the Akimbo takes some practice. Spend time on the ground and on low climbs learning how it holds, releases and handles changes in direction. Once you are used to it, many climbers find descents smoother and less tiring than tending a hitch all day.

Use only ropes within the rope types and diameters Rock Exotica lists for the device, and test any new rope low to the ground. Learn the device from the manufacturer's instructions and get training before you rely on it at height.
Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every use, and be used only by trained climbers working to ANSI Z133.
Inspect the device for wear on friction surfaces, cracks, loose parts and smooth function before each climb, and keep a record of its inspection history as part of your gear log.

faq.q: Can I use the Akimbo for both SRS and MRS?
faq.a: Yes. It is designed for both, but follow Rock Exotica's instructions for each configuration.

faq.q: What rope can I use?
faq.a: Use rope types and diameters within the manufacturer's listed range, and test a new rope near the ground first.

name: Yale R.I.N.G. Lanyard without Snaps
title: Yale R.I.N.G. Lanyard without Snaps
meta: Yale R.I.N.G. lanyard supplied without snaps, so you can choose your own connectors and adjuster. What to consider when you set it up and how to inspect it.
tagline: A Yale Cordage rope lanyard supplied without snaps so you choose your hardware.
summary: This Yale R.I.N.G. lanyard is supplied without snaps, so you can set it up with the connectors and adjuster that suit your climbing. It is a good option if you already have hardware you trust or want a custom setup.
highlights: Replace the rope, keep your hardware

body.h: Why buy a lanyard without snaps
p: A lot of climbers already own good carabiners or snaps and an adjuster they like. Buying the lanyard rope without hardware lets you replace a worn lanyard and move your trusted hardware across, or build a setup that matches how you work.
Make sure every connector you add is rated for life support and compatible with the lanyard's terminations. Other lanyards are in rope lanyards.

A rope lanyard is part of your work positioning system. It lets you lean back and work with both hands, and it is often your second point of attachment during cuts. That makes rope quality and the right terminations important, and Yale Cordage has a long history of making rope for tree work.

Set up and use the lanyard as Yale's instructions describe, and have a competent person check any custom configuration. Inspect the rope for cuts, glazing, stiff spots and wear at the terminations before every climb.
Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every use, and be used only by trained climbers working to ANSI Z133.

If you are not sure how to set up a lanyard without snaps, buy one with hardware fitted by the maker or a qualified supplier, or have an experienced climber help you put it together. A wrong termination is not something to find out about at height.

faq.q: What hardware do I need to add?
faq.a: Life-support rated connectors and, if you want adjustability, a compatible adjuster. Follow the lanyard maker's instructions for terminations.

faq.q: When should I retire a lanyard?
faq.a: Retire it if inspection shows cuts, heavy glazing, core damage, chainsaw contact or worn terminations, or when the maker's guidance says so.

name: Safewaze 6 ft Stretch Low Profile Shock Absorbing Lanyard
title: Safewaze Shock Absorbing Lanyard, 6 ft Stretch
h1: Safewaze Shock Absorbing Lanyard, 6 ft Stretch Low Profile
meta: Safewaze shock absorbing lanyard, 6 ft stretch style with a low-profile pack, for aerial lift and bucket truck fall protection. Fit and inspection notes.
tagline: A 6 ft stretch lanyard with a low-profile shock pack for bucket and lift work.
summary: The Safewaze shock absorbing lanyard is a 6 ft stretch design with a low-profile energy absorber, made for fall protection from aerial lifts and bucket trucks. The stretch webbing keeps slack down so it is less likely to snag around the bucket.
highlights: For aerial lift and bucket work
Connects to a full body harness

body.h: Why a stretch lanyard in the bucket
p: In a bucket or on a lift, a loose lanyard catches on controls and edges. Stretch webbing stays shorter at rest and extends as you move, so there is less loop hanging around. The low-profile shock pack sits close to your back instead of bouncing around.
Pair it with a full body harness and the anchor point your lift maker specifies. See the rest of our aerial lift fall arrest gear.

Low-profile packs are also more comfortable when you are leaning over the bucket edge to make a cut. A bulky absorber can catch on the bucket lip and pull at your harness, which is annoying at best. A slim pack stays out of the way and lets you work normally.
Follow the lift and lanyard makers' instructions and your company's fall protection program. Check required fall clearance, since a shock absorbing lanyard needs room to deploy.
Inspect webbing, stitching, the shock pack and the snap hooks before each use. Remove the lanyard from service if it has arrested a fall or shows damage, and get proper fall protection training.
Keep the lanyard clear of the chainsaw and any sharp edges on the bucket. Store it clean and dry, out of sunlight and away from chemicals and fuel.

faq.q: Can I use this for tree climbing?
faq.a: No. It is fall arrest equipment for aerial lifts and similar work. Tree climbing uses work positioning gear made for that purpose.

faq.q: What do I connect it to?
faq.a: The dorsal D-ring of a full body harness and the anchor point specified by the aerial lift manufacturer.

name: Safewaze Economy Full Body Harness
title: Safewaze Economy Full Body Harness
meta: Safewaze economy full body harness for fall protection in bucket trucks and aerial lifts. A simple, low-cost harness for crews. Fit and inspection notes.
tagline: A simple, low-cost full body harness for bucket truck and lift fall protection.
summary: The Safewaze economy full body harness is a simple fall protection harness for bucket truck and aerial lift work. It is a practical choice for outfitting crews who need a dependable harness for lift operators.
highlights: For aerial lift and bucket work

body.h: A harness for the lift, not the tree
p: A full body harness is fall arrest gear: it is meant to catch you and distribute the load if you fall from a lift. It is not a climbing saddle and is not made for work positioning in a tree. For bucket truck operators, it is the base of the fall protection system.
Pair it with a shock absorbing or restraint lanyard as required for your lift. More gear is in aerial lift fall arrest.

An economy harness keeps the basics: proper webbing, a dorsal D-ring and adjustable straps. It is a sensible choice where crews need several harnesses in the truck. Workers who spend all day in the bucket may want a harness with more padding for comfort.

Adjust leg, chest and shoulder straps so the harness fits snugly, with the dorsal D-ring between your shoulder blades. Follow the maker's fitting instructions and your company's fall protection program.
Inspect webbing, stitching, buckles and the D-ring before each use. Remove the harness from service after any fall or if you find damage, and make sure everyone wearing it is trained.
Store the harness clean and dry, away from fuel, chemicals and sunlight. Do not leave it balled up in the bottom of the bucket where tools and boots can damage it.

faq.q: Can I climb trees in this harness?
faq.a: No. Use an arborist climbing saddle for tree work. This harness is for fall arrest from lifts and similar platforms.

faq.q: What lanyard should I use?
faq.a: Use the lanyard type the lift manufacturer and your fall protection program call for, often a shock absorbing or restraint lanyard.

name: Arbortec Cobra DryKit Rope Bag 55L
title: Arbortec Cobra DryKit Rope Bag 55L
meta: Arbortec Cobra DryKit rope bag, 55L: a large bag that keeps rope and climbing kit dry and clean between jobs. Capacity, uses and care tips for tree crews.
tagline: A 55 liter DryKit bag that keeps rope and climbing kit clean and dry.
summary: The Arbortec Cobra DryKit rope bag is a 55L rope and gear bag that protects climbing kit from rain, mud and sawdust. It holds a climbing line plus a fair amount of hardware, so your kit travels as one load.
highlights: Keeps kit out of mud and sawdust

body.h: Protecting the gear you trust your life to
p: Grit and mud work into rope fibers and wear them from the inside. Sawdust and chain oil do your kit no favors either. A dry, closed rope bag keeps your climbing line and hardware clean on the truck and on the ground, which helps your gear last and makes inspection easier.
At 55 L there is room for a climbing line and a good share of your kit. See other options in gear bags.

A bag this size also helps with organization. When each climber's kit lives in its own bag, it is easier to see what you have, keep track of inspection, and avoid mixing personal life-support gear with the crew's general rigging equipment. That matters when you need to know the history of every piece you climb on.
Flake rope into the bag rather than coiling it, so it pays out without kinks. Keep sharp tools out of the rope bag. If your gear goes in wet, open the bag and let everything dry before storage.
Clean the bag inside and out from time to time. Store rope out of sunlight and away from fuel, oil and battery acid.
Check zips, seams and straps from time to time, and do not overload the bag so the handles and closure last longer.

faq.q: How much rope fits in a 55 L bag?
faq.a: It depends on rope diameter and how much other kit you pack. A typical climbing line plus some hardware fits comfortably.

faq.q: Can I store wet rope in it?
faq.a: Dry rope before long storage. A dry bag keeps water out, but it also keeps moisture in.

name: Helmet Liner Beanie, Sportflex
title: Sportflex Helmet Liner Beanie for Cold Weather
meta: Helmet liner beanie by Sportflex, a thin, warm layer that fits under a climbing or work helmet for cold-weather tree work. Fit, care and safety tips inside.
tagline: A thin beanie that fits under your helmet to keep your head warm in winter.
summary: The Sportflex helmet liner beanie is a thin, warm layer that fits under a climbing or work helmet. It keeps your head and ears warm on cold mornings without making the helmet sit poorly.
highlights: Thin enough to wear under a helmet

p: A regular winter hat is too thick to wear under a helmet; it pushes the helmet up and stops the harness fitting properly. A thin liner beanie gives you warmth without changing how the helmet sits. That matters on cold mornings in the tree and when you are standing at the chipper.
Browse other cold-weather hats in hats and caps.

Layering matters on winter jobs. You warm up quickly while climbing or dragging brush and then cool off fast when you stop. A thin liner traps less heat than a thick hat, so you are less likely to overheat on the climb and still have some warmth when you are standing still at the chipper.

After putting on the beanie, readjust your helmet's headband and chinstrap so it is snug and stable. If the helmet cannot be adjusted to fit properly over the liner, do not wear them together. Check your helmet maker's guidance on liners.
Wash the beanie regularly; sweat and sawdust build up fast. Air dry or follow the care label.
Keep a spare in your kit bag. A sweaty liner gets cold quickly, and swapping to a dry one at lunch makes the afternoon much more comfortable.

faq.q: Will this fit under my climbing helmet?
faq.a: It is thin enough for most helmets, but readjust the helmet afterward and make sure it still fits snugly.

faq.q: Does it work with ear muffs?
faq.a: A thin liner usually works, but check that ear cups still seal properly for full hearing protection.

name: Sterling BARC 2.0 Rigging Web Chain
title: Sterling BARC 2.0 Rigging Web Chain
meta: Sterling BARC 2.0 rigging web chain: a webbing sling with multiple connection points for adjustable rigging anchors and attachments. Uses and inspection.
tagline: A multi-loop webbing sling for adjustable rigging anchors and attachments.
summary: The Sterling BARC 2.0 rigging web chain is a webbing sling with a series of loops, giving you several connection points along its length. Riggers use a web chain to set an anchor or attach to a piece at the length they need without tying knots.
highlights: No knots to tie or untie

body.h: How a web chain helps rigging
p: Wrapping an anchor or a piece of wood with a fixed-length sling often leaves you with too much or too little tail. A web chain gives you a choice of loops, so you can choke or basket around different diameters and clip in at the right length. It is quick to set and quick to remove when the piece is down.
Check the working load and choking ratings on the label and in Sterling's instructions. More slings are in heavy-duty slings.

Webbing slings are lighter than rope slings of similar strength and lie flatter on the stem, which some riggers prefer for wrapping trunks and spars. A web chain adds flexibility on top of that, which is useful when you are rigging on stems of varying size during a removal.

Rigging loads can be far higher than the weight of the piece once it is moving. Plan the rig, use components with matching ratings, and keep slings away from sharp edges and chainsaw chain. Follow ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions.
Inspect the webbing and stitching before each use for cuts, abrasion, heat damage and chemical contamination. Retire a sling that is damaged or has taken a shock load beyond its rating.
Store slings clean and dry, out of sunlight, and keep a record of their use along with the rest of your rigging gear.

faq.q: Can I use a web chain for climbing?
faq.a: Use it only as the manufacturer allows. Rigging slings should not be used for life support unless they are rated and marked for it.

faq.q: How do I choose which loop to clip?
faq.a: Pick the loop that gives the length you need without twisting the webbing, and follow Sterling's guidance for choking and basket hitches.

name: Visor for LAND AeroPro and ClimbPro Helmets
title: LAND Helmet Visor for AeroPro and ClimbPro
h1: LAND Helmet Visor for AeroPro and ClimbPro Helmets
meta: LAND helmet visor for AeroPro and ClimbPro helmets. Replace a scratched or broken visor to keep chips and sawdust out of your face. Fit and care notes.
tagline: A replacement face visor for LAND AeroPro and ClimbPro helmets.
summary: This LAND helmet visor fits AeroPro and ClimbPro helmets, so you can replace a scratched, cracked or lost visor and keep your helmet system complete. A clear view matters when you are working a saw.
highlights: Replaces a scratched or broken visor
Helps keep chips out of your face

p: Visors get scratched from sawdust, wiping, and being tossed around the truck. A scratched visor makes it harder to see the chain, the cut and the line. Cracked or broken visors stop giving protection. Replacing the visor costs far less than a new helmet.
Check that your helmet is an AeroPro or ClimbPro before ordering. Related protection is in hearing protection.

A visor is also useful for ground workers feeding the chipper or bucking logs, where chips fly toward the face. Keeping the visor in good shape means you are more likely to wear it down, rather than flipping it up because you cannot see through it.

A mesh or face visor helps with chips and debris, but it is not a substitute for safety glasses where eye protection is required. Wear rated eyewear under the visor as your job and ANSI Z133 call for.
Clean the visor gently with water and a soft cloth. Avoid solvents and rough rags that scratch. Inspect the visor and its mount regularly and replace them when damaged.
Keep a spare visor in your kit if you work a saw daily. Replacing one on the job only takes a couple of minutes and means you are not working with a bad view for the rest of the day.

faq.q: Do I still need safety glasses?
faq.a: Yes, where eye protection is required. A visor helps with debris but does not replace rated safety eyewear.

faq.q: Will it fit other helmets?
faq.a: It is made for LAND AeroPro and ClimbPro helmets. Check your helmet model before ordering.

name: Estex Polycomb Insert for 1-Man Bucket Truck Cover
title: Estex Polycomb Insert for 1-Man Bucket Cover
h1: Estex Polycomb Insert for 1-Man Bucket Truck Cover
meta: Estex Polycomb insert for 1-man bucket truck covers. It adds stiffness so the cover keeps its shape and protects the bucket. Fit and care notes here.
tagline: A stiff Polycomb insert that helps a 1-man Estex bucket cover hold its shape.
summary: The Estex Polycomb insert is a stiff panel made for 1-man bucket truck covers. It adds structure so the cover stays in shape and protects the bucket liner from rain, debris and sun when the truck is parked or on the road.
highlights: Helps the cover keep its shape
Protects the bucket from debris and weather

p: A bucket cover keeps rain, leaves and sawdust out of the bucket between jobs and while driving. Without a stiff panel, a cover can sag and fill with water. The Polycomb insert gives the cover structure, so it sheds water and stays put.
Make sure your cover is a 1-man Estex model. More bucket gear is in bucket truck accessories.

A well-kept cover also stops water and leaves building up in the bucket, which keeps the floor cleaner and less slippery when you climb in. Polycomb is a honeycomb-style panel that is light and stiff, so it supports the cover without making it heavy to take on and off.
Slide the insert into the cover as Estex describes and check the cover still fastens securely to the bucket. Secure the cover before driving so it cannot blow off.

Clean debris off the cover regularly and inspect the insert for cracks. Remember that covers and inserts are not part of the bucket's dielectric protection; keep the bucket liner and boom inspected and tested as your utility program requires.

If your existing insert is cracked or warped, the cover will sag and let water in. Replacing the insert is a cheap way to bring an older cover back into working shape without buying a whole new cover.

faq.q: Does this include the cover?
faq.a: No. This is the Polycomb insert for an existing 1-man bucket cover.

faq.q: Will it fit a 2-man bucket cover?
faq.a: It is sized for 1-man covers. Check your bucket and cover size before ordering.

name: Safewaze D-Ring Extender
title: Safewaze D-Ring Extender for Fall Harnesses
meta: Safewaze D-ring extender makes it easier to clip a lanyard to the back D-ring of a full body harness. How it is used, what to check and how it fits a system.
tagline: A short extension that brings your harness back D-ring within easy reach.
summary: The Safewaze D-ring extender is a short webbing extension for the dorsal D-ring on a full body harness. It makes it easier to clip and unclip a lanyard yourself, which is handy for lift operators who connect many times a day.
highlights: Easier to clip your own lanyard

p: The back D-ring on a full body harness sits between your shoulder blades, which is the right place for fall arrest but awkward to reach. An extender brings the connection point up and out so you can hook up without help. Lift operators connecting and disconnecting through the day notice the difference.
Pair it with the right lanyard and harness. See the rest of our aerial lift fall arrest gear.

An extender also helps when a worker wears a harness with limited mobility or bulky winter clothing, where reaching behind the shoulders is hard. Being able to connect and disconnect yourself reliably means you are more likely to stay tied in throughout the job, which is the point of a fall protection system.
An extender adds length to your fall arrest system, which increases the required fall clearance. Factor it into your calculations and follow Safewaze's instructions on compatible lanyards.
Inspect the webbing, stitching and hardware before each use. Remove it from service after a fall or if you find damage, and make sure users are trained in fall protection.
Store the extender with the harness and lanyard, clean and dry, and keep it away from chemicals, fuel and sharp edges.

faq.q: Does an extender change fall clearance?
faq.a: Yes. It adds length, so include it in your fall clearance calculation.

faq.q: Can I use it with any lanyard?
faq.a: Follow the manufacturer's compatibility guidance. Some energy absorbers are not meant to be used with extenders.

name: Safewaze Energy Absorbing Lanyard with Soft Eye
title: Safewaze Energy Absorbing Lanyard with Soft Eye
h1: Safewaze Energy Absorbing Lanyard with Soft Eye
meta: Safewaze energy absorbing lanyard with a soft eye end that girth hitches to a harness or anchor. For aerial lift fall protection. Fit and inspection notes here.
tagline: An energy absorbing lanyard with a soft eye that girth hitches to your harness.
summary: The Safewaze energy absorbing lanyard with soft eye uses a sewn loop on one end instead of a hook, so it can be girth hitched to a harness or anchor. It is designed to limit forces on your body if you fall from an aerial lift.
highlights: Soft eye end for girth hitching
Snap hook on the anchor end

p: A soft eye is a sewn loop that you girth hitch to a harness attachment or anchor. It removes one metal connector from the system, which keeps the lanyard lighter and lower profile. The energy absorber tears out in a fall to limit the load on your body and the anchor.
Check how your harness and anchor accept a soft eye before ordering. Related gear is in aerial lift fall arrest.

Some workers prefer soft eye lanyards because they cannot be accidentally unclipped from the harness end, and there is less metal against the back. They are also lighter. The tradeoff is that changing a girth-hitched lanyard takes a little longer than unclipping a snap hook.

Connect only as Safewaze's instructions describe, and check required fall clearance, since an absorber needs room to deploy. Follow the lift maker's anchor instructions and your fall protection program.
Inspect the webbing, soft eye, stitching, absorber pack and snap hook before each use. Remove the lanyard from service after a fall or if it shows damage. Users need fall protection training.
Store the lanyard clean and dry and keep it out of sunlight. Do not tie knots in it or wrap it around sharp edges.

faq.q: How do I attach a soft eye?
faq.a: Usually by girth hitching it to an approved harness or anchor point, as the manufacturer's instructions show.

faq.q: Can it be reused after a fall?
faq.a: No. Remove any energy absorbing lanyard from service after it has arrested a fall.
